zebralogic.title: Assign fixed‑position attributes immediately
zebralogic.principle: If a clue directly ties a specific attribute value to a house number, place that attribute in that house right away. This reduces the search space and prevents later contradictions.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue mentions a specific house number for an attribute (e.g., "the fifth house", "house 6").
zebralogic.example: Delaying the placement of a fixed‑position attribute and later assigning a different value to that house, causing a conflict.

zebralogic.title: Translate direct adjacency into offset constraints
zebralogic.principle: Clues using "directly left of" or "directly right of" mean the two houses are adjacent with a known direction; encode this as pos(right) = pos(left) + 1 (or the reverse).
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue contains the phrase "directly left of" or "directly right of".
zebralogic.example: Treating "directly left of" as just "somewhere left of" and allowing any gap between the houses.

zebralogic.title: Interpret distance clues correctly
zebralogic.principle: A clue stating "N houses between X and Y" means there are exactly N houses separating them, i.e., |pos(X) – pos(Y)| = N + 1.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue mentions a specific number of houses between two attributes.
zebralogic.example: Interpreting "two houses between" as a distance of two instead of three, placing the two attributes only two houses apart.

zebralogic.title: Bind equivalence clues to the same house
zebralogic.principle: If a clue equates two (or more) attributes, they must occupy the same house; treat them as interchangeable for all other constraints.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue states that two attributes belong to the same person (e.g., "Alice drinks blueberry smoothies" or "the bird owner drinks blueberry smoothies").
zebralogic.example: Assigning the blueberry smoothie to Alice but forgetting to also assign the bird pet to Alice, violating the equivalence.

zebralogic.title: Treat "somewhere left/right of" as inequality
zebralogic.principle: Clues that say X is somewhere to the left/right of Y impose only an ordering (pos(X) < pos(Y) or pos(X) > pos(Y)); adjacency is allowed but not required.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue uses phrasing like "somewhere to the left of", "somewhere right of", or "to the left of" without the word "directly".
zebralogic.example: Assuming X must be at least two houses away from Y when the clue only says "somewhere left of".

zebralogic.title: Apply exclusion constraints
zebralogic.principle: If a clue forbids an attribute from a particular house, record that prohibition and never place that attribute there.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue explicitly says an attribute is not in a given house (e.g., "the rose bouquet is not in the sixth house").
zebralogic.example: Placing the rose flower in house 6 despite the clue stating it cannot be there.

zebralogic.title: Enforce uniqueness across each attribute category
zebralogic.principle: Each value in a category must appear exactly once; after assigning a value to a house, remove it from the pool of possible values for the remaining houses.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Throughout the solving process, after any assignment.
zebralogic.example: Assigning the same nationality to two different houses, violating the one‑per‑category rule.

zebralogic.title: Disambiguate overlapping attribute values across categories
zebralogic.principle: When a term appears in more than one attribute category, keep the categories separate and never mix them; treat each occurrence according to its category.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When parsing clues that mention a word that could belong to multiple categories (e.g., "bird" as a pet, "blueberry" as a smoothie).
zebralogic.example: Treating the word "bird" as a flower instead of a pet.

zebralogic.title: Preserve original case of attribute values
zebralogic.principle: Output attribute values exactly as they appear in the problem statement, preserving capitalization and spelling, to avoid mismatches with the verifier.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When constructing the final JSON solution.
zebralogic.example: Outputting "alice" instead of "Alice", causing a case mismatch.

zebralogic.title: Interpret "next to each other" as bidirectional adjacency
zebralogic.principle: Clues stating that two entities are "next to each other" mean they occupy adjacent houses, but the order is not fixed; either could be left or right.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue uses phrasing like "next to each other" or "are next to each other".
zebralogic.example: Assuming X must be left of Y when the clue only says they are next to each other, ignoring the opposite ordering.

zebralogic.description: Treating "somewhere left of" as adjacency (directly left)
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model confuses the non‑specific ordering phrase with the explicit adjacency phrase because both mention "left of".
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Remember that "somewhere left of" only imposes an ordering; adjacency is required only when the clue says "directly left of" or "directly right of".

zebralogic.description: Interpreting "N houses between" as distance N
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model forgets that the count of houses between excludes the two houses themselves, so the positional difference is N + 1.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Add one to the given number when converting a "N houses between" clue to an absolute positional difference.

zebralogic.description: Ignoring equivalence clues that bind two attributes to the same house
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model treats each attribute independently and does not propagate the equivalence across other constraints.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Whenever a clue equates two attributes, record them as a single combined entity for that house and apply all other constraints to that entity.

zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model does not keep a global record of which values have already been used in each category.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: After placing a value, remove it from the list of possible values for the remaining houses in that category.

zebralogic.description: Assuming a fixed direction for "next to each other" clues
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model assumes the first mentioned entity is left of the second, even though the clue only guarantees adjacency.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Treat "next to each other" as unordered adjacency; consider both possible left‑right orders when applying the constraint.
